maria: Heads-up — ran the initial bring-up for Lite9B-int6 (sideloaded weights) against the GTN chat slices. Quick summary below and a couple of asks.

jon: Nice. can you drop the raw numbers?

maria: Sure. Short scorecard: 
```
Model: Lite9B-int6 (sideload)
Slices: chat-short, chat-long, instruction-clarity
Quality: chat-short = 92.1% QA-accuracy, chat-long = 84.3% QA-accuracy
Latency: p50=42ms, p95=190ms (single-request), p99=420ms
Unit cost: token-cost = $0.0018 / 1k tokens (estimated), avg tokens per request = 260
Throughput: 45 req/s on 2xA10g w/ continuous batching
Regression: vs baseline Nova7B-int8 => -1.8% on longform recall (not huge)
```

keith: latency p99 looks high — is that warm-start tail or kvcache churn?

maria: Tail is mostly kvcache misses on long sequences. We saw a correlation with concurrent small-batched requests. When we force single-request cold starts p99 goes to ~670ms.

nora: From product POV: what is the lift vs current production model and is the cost saving worth the small recall drop?

maria: Compared to Prod-Nova7B-int8: cost per token is ~20% lower, p50 is ~1.1x faster, but longform recall drops ~1.8 pts for the instruction-clarity slice. For chat-short the score is parity.

jon: Can you paste the per-slice delta table?

maria: Here: 
```
Slice, Prod(Nova7B-int8) QA, Lite9B-int6 QA, Delta, Cost per 1k tokens
chat-short, 92.3, 92.1, -0.2, $0.0023 -> $0.0018
chat-long, 86.1, 84.3, -1.8, $0.0023 -> $0.0018
instruction-clarity, 88.9, 87.1, -1.8, $0.0023 -> $0.0018
```

jon: Ok. Notable that both long slices drop similarly. Might be quantization sensitivity for long-context attention.

keith: Ops note: on Dedicated we could reduce p99 by enabling warm-KV pinned workers for long sessions. That will add ~8% infra cost but cut tail in half.

nora: So we should weigh infra bump vs token cost savings. If infra + token cost still lower, might be a net win. Any estimates?

maria: Quick calc: token savings ~20% on cost-per-token. For our sample traffic mix (60% chat-short, 30% chat-long, 10% instruction), net token cost savings = ~18%. Adding warm-KV reserved capacity (+8% infra) yields net platform cost reduction ~10-11%.

jon: What about quality regression mitigation? Any prompt-level fixes?

maria: We tried simple priming tweaks and 2-shot anchors for long-context — improved recall by ~0.6-0.9 pts but not fully recovered. Suspect kernel-level attention precision loss.

keith: Are there any compat quant profiles we can try (int6 alternative packing) that trade a bit of throughput for quality?

maria: Yes — we ran two variants: int6-fast (packed aggressive) and int6-safe (wider accumulator). int6-safe recovered ~1.2 pts on longform but increased p50 by 8% and increased token-cost equivalent by ~6% due to throughput hit.

nora: Pragmatic recommendation options?

maria: Three options: 
1) Roll Lite9B-int6 with warm-KV reserved workers, route 60% chat-short, 0% chat-long initially, keep Prod-Nova for long until deeper quantization work — immediate cost savings but conservative on longform.
2) Roll int6-safe globally with warm-KV — recovers quality nearly parity, net cost savings ~6-7%. More conservative and single model across slices.
3) Hold on Lite9B until we run int6-ivp (improved kernel) — no immediate savings, but less risk.

jon: My vote is option 2 for a staged roll if we can run a 2-week canary on 10% traffic and track recall/regression signals.

keith: I'll prototype the warm-KV reserved pool config and estimate infra delta more precisely. Will post numbers by EOD.

maria: Also created an eval-bot run for canary that reports per-prompt sentinel failure. eval-bot, kick off canary-signal?

eval-bot: Canary started — 5k synthetic chats + 2k longform runs. Will publish daily deltas to /canary/lite9b-int6.

nora: Thanks. action items: keith infra estimate, jon -> canary metric thresholds, maria -> int6-safe build + priming recipes. I'll sync with sales/GTN on expected price messaging if we move forward. :thumbsup:

jon: threshold suggestion: rollback if any slice drops >1.0 absolute QA-accuracy or p99 latency worsens by >30% versus baseline for 24h.

maria: noted. I'll post the first canary snapshot tomorrow morning.

keith: ETA infra numbers by 5pm PT.

nora: perfect — we'll reconvene after the first snapshot.

maria: uploading raw logs and the lightweight scorecard to the team drive: https://redwood.team/lite9b-int6/canary-brief

jon: thanks all.

maria: tl;dr: Lite9B-int6 looks promising for chat-short; longform needs either int6-safe or warm-KV reserved workers to be product-ready. Recommend staged canary for option 2. :white_check_mark:
